articles.standfirst: The Mexican boxer confirms that he will keep his highly anticipated fight in Riyadh against Christian M"Billi despite the recent military attacks in the country's capital
articles.summary: The Mexican boxer confirms that he will keep his highly anticipated fight in Riyadh against Christian M"Billi despite the recent military attacks in the country's capital
articles.body:
The world of professional boxing is on maximum alert after the serious war-related events recorded on Saudi territory . However, Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez has made a drastic decision about the immediate future of his boxing career.

Despite the recent projectile and drone attacks reported near the capital, the champion from Guadalajara has no intention whatsoever of canceling or relocating his next sporting commitment . The event is scheduled as the headline clash of a night of major international impact.

This decision has surprised analysts and fans of combat sports, who were speculating about an inevitable cancellation or rescheduling given the complex security situation in the Middle East .

A direct call to clear up any doubts

The person in charge of confirming the stance of the fighter from Jalisco was Sheikh Turki Alalshikh himself, president of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority and one of the most influential promoters on the world circuit . As the official explained on his official channels, it was the Mexican boxer who took the initiative to contact him directly to reassure him .

Alalshikh stated that Canelo told him in no uncertain terms of his intention to step into the ring next October 31 at Riyadh's Kingdom Arena, "no matter what happens" . The Saudi official praised the Aztec pugilist's bravery, publicly stating that the fighter "is not afraid of anything" and stressing that difficult times serve to identify true friendships .

The promoter's statements seek to ease the uncertainty surrounding the evening called "Mexico against the World" . The organization maintains that the venue has all the necessary guarantees to host a massive event on a global scale .

A turbulent scenario and the warning from the embassies

The announcement comes at an extremely delicate time after impacts were confirmed near key facilities in the Saudi capital , including an attack in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. Various international media outlets, including the British newspaper The Guardian, reported a tragic toll with fatalities and dozens of injuries following the explosions .

Given this situation of instability, organizations such as the United States Mission in Saudi Arabia issued security alerts recommending that their citizens exercise extreme caution and remain attentive to notices from the local Civil Defense . For their part, specialized commentators such as Luke Thomas or analyst Dan Canobbio even went so far as to call it reckless to organize a fight card in an area affected by direct war-related tensions.

However, the Aztec boxer's team, led by his trainer Eddy Reynoso, has chosen to keep the training plan unchanged . To optimize his acclimatization, Canelo completed part of his training camp in Gandía, Spain, seeking to reduce the impact of the time difference before permanently relocating to the Persian Gulf .

The long-awaited recapture of the super middleweight throne

On a strictly sporting level, the clash against French-Cameroonian Christian M"Billi represents a crucial challenge in the fighter from Guadalajara's career. It will be Canelo Álvarez's first appearance since his painful defeat to American Terence Crawford in September 2025 , a setback in which he relinquished his status as the undisputed 168-pound champion.

His opponent, known in boxing circles as "Solide," arrives at this event undefeated and holds the World Boxing Council (WBC) belt . M"Billi is recognized for his aggressive style and an incessant volume of punches, qualities that promise to deliver an extremely physical contest in the ring.

For this reason, the clash in Riyadh not only entails taking on a turbulent geopolitical environment, but also the opportunity to prove that the Mexican idol still belongs to the absolute elite of world boxing .

The history of sporting events in conflict zones

The decision to fight amid a turbulent wartime climate is not entirely unprecedented in the history of combat sports, although it does constitute a highly unusual event in the modern era. Boxing historians quickly recall the legendary 1974 "Rumble in the Jungle" bout between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in Kinshasa, Zaire, held under enormous regional political uncertainty.

In more recent times, promoters and international organizations have chosen to relocate venues at any sign of geopolitical or health instability in order to preserve the safety of athletes and fans. An emblematic case occurred in 2021 during the bout between Teófimo López and George Kambosos Jr. , which underwent multiple reschedulings and venue changes before finally taking place in New York.

In the case of Canelo Álvarez , the substantial purses and the contractual commitments signed with the Saudi authorities have weighed decisively in keeping the date . At the end of this month, the ring in Riyadh will deliver its sporting verdict under the watchful eyes of the entire planet.

articles.title: Jake Paul's latest boxing stunt backfires as fans react to disturbing snake footage
articles.standfirst: Viral training session prompted concern about animal welfare rather than excitement over potential comeback.
articles.summary: Viral training session prompted concern about animal welfare rather than excitement over potential comeback.
articles.body:
Jake Paul has spent years finding unconventional ways to attract attention, but his latest appearance in a boxing gym has left some fans more concerned about an animal than his potential return to the boxing ring.

The 29-year-old appeared in a video shared by boxing social media account Happy Punch, showing him working around a heavy bag with a large snake wrapped around the chain above it.

The animal, believed to be a python, remained close to the bag as Paul circled cautiously, occasionally throwing punches while watching its movements.

An unidentified person could be heard giving instructions from off camera, telling Paul to "start jabbing around it" as he attempted to continue the exercise.

The footage lasted approximately 40 seconds, but quickly generated criticism from viewers who questioned the decision to involve a live animal in boxing training.

Putting snake under unnecessary stress

Rather than focusing on Paul 's technique, much of the reaction centered on whether the snake was being subjected to unnecessary distress.

"Bro, this is just animal abuse," one social media user wrote, while another questioned the apparent purpose of the exercise.

"The f**k did the snake do to him? This is trashy man," another viewer commented, reflecting the frustration expressed by several people responding to the footage.

Others accused Paul of using the animal primarily to generate attention, suggesting the unusual setup offered little practical benefit to his preparations.

Paul hasn't provided a detailed public explanation of the session, leaving questions about whether the exercise was intended as legitimate training or simply entertainment.

Controversy follows Paul after Joshua knockout

The backlash comes as Paul considers returning to boxing following his defeat against former heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua in December 2025.

Joshua knocked Paul out in the sixth round of their Miami contest, leaving the American with a broken jaw that subsequently required multiple surgeries.

That defeat reignited debate about Paul 's credentials, particularly after years of criticism concerning the age and competitive backgrounds of several previous opponents.

One viewer referenced the loss while responding to the snake footage, asking, "How is this going to help his glass jaw?"

Another sarcastically remarked, "So stunning and brave," questioning whether the exercise demonstrated anything meaningful about Paul's boxing abilities.

Paul's next move remains unclear

Paul has suggested that a return to competition could happen in early 2027, although no opponent or official date has been confirmed.

He has also expressed interest in professional football and discussed potential future fights, including another possible venture into mixed martial arts.

Unusual training content is not entirely new territory for Paul , who previously shared footage involving his Golden Retriever, Thor, whom he jokingly described as a boxing coach.

The latest video, however, has generated a different response because it involves a snake positioned directly beside a moving heavy bag.

Whether intended as entertainment or preparation, the footage has shifted attention away from Paul 's comeback ambitions and toward questions about the treatment of animals during promotional boxing content.

articles.title: Trump taps Floyd Mayweather for Arizona rally as campaign leans on star athletes
articles.standfirst: Mayweather's planned appearance follows years of public support for Trump and comes ahead of November's midterm elections
articles.summary: Mayweather's planned appearance follows years of public support for Trump and comes ahead of November's midterm elections
articles.body:
President Donald Trump is bringing another familiar face from the boxing world into his election campaign, with Floyd Mayweather Jr. reportedly preparing to accompany the president to Arizona on Wednesday.

The undefeated former boxing world champion is expected to board Air Force One in Las Vegas before traveling to Bullhead City, where Trump is holding a rally to support Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

According to the Daily Mail, Mayweather , 49, will attend the event, although it remains uncertain whether he will address supporters or simply join the president as a guest.

The planned appearance comes amid a series of campaign events featuring well-known athletes, demonstrating how frequently sporting personalities have become part of Trump's public appearances.

Mayweather 's association with Trump predates the president's current campaign schedule, with the former boxer having attended his first inauguration in January 2017.

The five-division world champion has remained publicly supportive of Trump , expressing particular admiration for his business background during a February 2025 appearance on Fox Business.

Speaking on Making Money with Charles Payne, Mayweather delivered an enthusiastic assessment of the president's record.

"When we had Trump before, we didn't appreciate him. But I think Trump is a great president, one of the, actually he's the best president," Mayweather said. "In my eyes, he's the best president we ever had."

Mayweather also praised Trump 's experience in business, an area where the former fighter has developed his own extensive interests since retiring from professional boxing.

"Great business, great businessman, and that's what it's about," Mayweather added during the interview.

His comments attracted attention beyond political circles, including criticism from rapper 50 Cent , with whom Mayweather has maintained a longstanding public feud.

Mike Tyson and Jake Paul in Trump's recent rallies

Mayweather would follow another former heavyweight boxing champion, Mike Tyson , who accompanied Trump on a recent trip to Syracuse, New York.

During that appearance, the president spotted Tyson among the audience and invited him onto the stage to speak.

"Thank you, thank you very much. I'm just happy to be up here with my president, President Trump," Tyson told supporters.

"There's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump."

The president has also appeared alongside former NBA star Dennis Rodman , retired NFL coach Jon Gruden and boxer-turned-social media personality Jake Paul .

Baseball legend Roger Clemens attended another event in San Antonio, where Trump announced his intention to award the former pitcher the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

Why Arizona is important stop for Trump campaign

The Bullhead City rally forms part of a broader campaign effort to support Republican candidates before voters head to the polls next month.

Trump is visiting Arizona to back Andy Biggs , who is challenging Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs in the state's gubernatorial election.

The president is also scheduled to campaign in Montana, continuing a series of appearances across western states as both parties compete for support ahead of the midterms.

Mayweather 's connection to Arizona extends beyond politics through his business interests, giving the former boxer an additional link to Wednesday's destination.

His planned appearance adds another chapter to a relationship that has lasted nearly a decade, although whether he will take the microphone remains to be seen.

articles.summary: Fundora wants to reaffirm his championship.
articles.body:
"S ebastian Fundora returns to the ring this Saturday, October 17, to defend his WBC super welterweight world championship against Ermal Hadribeaj , in a fight that promises plenty of excitement for boxing fans, as these are two serious fighters. Fundora wants to establish himself as champion, but his rival will have the final say.

Hadribeaj, who comes into this fight as the challenger, is facing the biggest opportunity of his career as he could take the title away from Fundora, but to do so he will have to deliver a practically perfect fight. Below at MARCA MX we tell you the details of this matchup.

It should be remembered that this bout will take place at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas , a venue located within the The Cosmopolitan, in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States complex. Attendance of more than 3 thousand spectators is expected at this venue.

How do Sebastian Fundora and Ermal Hadribeaj arrive at the WBC world title fight?

Sebastian Fundora , who stands out for his height in the super welterweight division, comes in as the defending champion with a professional record of 24 wins, one loss, and one draw, including 16 victories by knockout. At 28 years old, the 1.97-meter American aims to retain his belt and move closer to potential unification bouts during 2027.

On the other hand, Ermal Hadribeaj arrives as the mandatory challenger with an undefeated record of 23 wins and one draw, along with eight knockouts. The 32-year-old Albanian boxer, standing 1.78 meters tall, will face a significant physical disadvantage, although he will look to make up for it with mobility and constant pressure.

It is a matchup between boxers with different styles, which is why it has drawn a lot of attention in the boxing world, in addition to being an unprecedented fight, since it is the first time they have faced each other.

Sebastian Fundora vs Ermal Hadribeaj, who is the favorite?

According to the information reviewed, Sebastian Fundora comes in as the favorite for this matchup due to his experience and reach, in addition to his dominant style that always seeks to pressure his opponents.

The forecast indicates that the American could win the fight by technical knockout and retain his WBC super welterweight championship next Saturday.

However, anything can happen in a championship fight.

articles.title: Floyd Mayweather is being heavily criticized for supporting President Donald Trump at a rally in Arizona
articles.standfirst: The undefeated boxing legend has sparked fresh debate after praising Donald Trump during a political rally in Bullhead City, Arizona
articles.summary: The undefeated boxing legend has sparked fresh debate after praising Donald Trump during a political rally in Bullhead City, Arizona
articles.body:
F loyd Mayweather has found himself at the centre of another social media storm after publicly endorsing President Donald Trump during a rally in Arizona.

The former five-division world champion addressed the crowd in Bullhead City on October 14, expressing his admiration for the United States and describing Trump as the right person to lead the country.

Mayweather's appearance attracted attention beyond the political event itself. Clips of his speech circulated online, prompting a mixture of supportive reactions, jokes and criticism from boxing fans.

Some questioned why the retired fighter had chosen to participate in the rally, while others targeted his intelligence and personal life rather than focusing on his political message.

One reaction shared after footage of Mayweather and Trump circulated online read: “Those hits to the head are catching up lol.”

The comment reflected the mocking tone adopted by some users, although it does not establish anything about Mayweather's health. The criticism instead illustrates how the boxer's public persona often attracts as much attention as his sporting achievements.

During his address, Mayweather spoke about representing the United States at the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta before praising Trump's presidency.

“America is the best country in the world,” Mayweather said. “If I died and came back a million times, I will always choose America. It was great to represent this country in the 1996 Olympic Games to go out there and represent the red, white, and blue.

“And we can…we couldn’t have chosen a better president twice than Donald Trump . So, it’s all about keeping this country strong, and it’s all about us sticking together and believing in one another. America is the best country in the world. Thank you.”

The speech made his position clear, but the reaction demonstrated how divisive celebrity involvement in politics can be.

Mayweather's words about national pride were accompanied by an explicit endorsement of Trump, giving critics a fresh opportunity to debate the boxer's public influence.

Why Mayweather's support for Trump is drawing criticism

The Arizona appearance was not the first time Mayweather had praised the president. In February 2025, the boxing star appeared on Fox Business and described Trump as a great president and businessman, explaining that he admired the president's approach to business and leadership.

"Trump is a great president," he said. "He's the best president in my eyes, a great businessman. And that's what it's about."

Mayweather's latest remarks therefore continue a position he has expressed publicly before, rather than representing a sudden change of political direction.

His comments have also come amid a wider trend of athletes and entertainers appearing alongside political figures, where celebrity endorsements can attract attention from audiences who might not otherwise follow a campaign.

However, some online responses focused less on Trump's policies and more on Mayweather himself.

“Floyd isn’t very high IQ outside the boxing ring,” one fan wrote.

Another user commented: “This mf can’t even read. I’m not listening to him,” while a separate reaction stated, “You know it’s from the heart since he can’t read from the teleprompter.”

The remarks refer to a long-running online narrative about Mayweather's reading ability. His former associate, rapper 50 Cent, has repeatedly mocked him over the issue, including challenging him to read a page from a Harry Potter book on camera.

That personal feud has helped keep the subject alive on social media, even though it has little bearing on Mayweather's achievements as a professional boxer.

Other comments were more direct in questioning his influence. “The last person anybody’s gonna listen to is Floyd Mayweather ,” one user wrote.

Another added, “Is anyone really listening to Floyd? He’s a grandpa walking around with tons of cash trying to impress…Grow up, my guy.”

Such reactions show how Mayweather's enormous sporting profile has not necessarily translated into universal respect for his views outside boxing.

His supporters may see his appearance as an expression of personal freedom and patriotism, while critics argue that celebrity endorsements invite scrutiny, particularly when they involve controversial political figures.

Mayweather's boxing legacy and troubles outside the ring

Mayweather's sporting achievements remain difficult to dispute. He retired from professional boxing with an undefeated 50-0 record, having beaten a long list of prominent opponents during a career that included championship victories across multiple weight divisions.

His defensive technique, timing and ability to control fights made him one of the defining boxers of his generation.

He has remained involved in boxing since his professional retirement in 2017, particularly through exhibition events. Yet his plans for further appearances have encountered complications in 2026.

An exhibition against Greek kickboxing star Mike Zambidis , scheduled for June in Athens, was called off amid a legal dispute involving CSI Sports Events.

The company alleged that Mayweather's agreements to fight Mike Tyson and Manny Pacquiao created contractual restrictions on competing in other events first.

Those claims were part of a legal dispute, rather than a finding that Mayweather had committed wrongdoing. The proposed Pacquiao rematch was also pushed into uncertainty.

Mayweather has also faced scrutiny over financial matters. In April 2026, The Ring reported that the IRS had notified him of its intention to alert the State Department about a possible passport revocation related to an unresolved tax debt. That development threatened to complicate his international exhibition plans.

Those issues have contributed to the broader attention surrounding Mayweather , although they are separate from his political endorsement.

The fact that he continues to attract headlines across sport, business and politics reflects his unusual position as a globally recognised athlete whose public life extends far beyond the ring.

Ultimately, Mayweather's appearance in Arizona has reopened the debate over how much influence celebrities should wield in political conversations. His supporters are entitled to view his endorsement as a personal expression of patriotism, while critics remain free to challenge his judgment and political choices.

The backlash may continue online, but it does not change the central point: Mayweather has made his support for Trump public, and the reaction shows that his words still command attention.

Why Mayweather's support for Trump is drawing criticism

The Arizona appearance was not the first time Mayweather had praised the president. In February 2025, the boxing star appeared on Fox Business and described Trump as a great president and businessman, explaining that he admired the president's approach to business and leadership.
"Trump is a great president," he said. "He's the best president in my eyes, a great businessman. And that's what it's about."
Mayweather's latest remarks therefore continue a position he has expressed publicly before, rather than representing a sudden change of political direction.

His comments have also come amid a wider trend of athletes and entertainers appearing alongside political figures, where celebrity endorsements can attract attention from audiences who might not otherwise follow a campaign.
However, some online responses focused less on Trump's policies and more on Mayweather himself.
“Floyd isn’t very high IQ outside the boxing ring,” one fan wrote.
Another user commented: “This mf can’t even read. I’m not listening to him,” while a separate reaction stated, “You know it’s from the heart since he can’t read from the teleprompter.”

The remarks refer to a long-running online narrative about Mayweather's reading ability. His former associate, rapper 50 Cent, has repeatedly mocked him over the issue, including challenging him to read a page from a Harry Potter book on camera.
That personal feud has helped keep the subject alive on social media, even though it has little bearing on Mayweather's achievements as a professional boxer.
Other comments were more direct in questioning his influence. “The last person anybody’s gonna listen to is Floyd Mayweather ,” one user wrote.
Another added, “Is anyone really listening to Floyd? He’s a grandpa walking around with tons of cash trying to impress…Grow up, my guy.”
Such reactions show how Mayweather's enormous sporting profile has not necessarily translated into universal respect for his views outside boxing.

His supporters may see his appearance as an expression of personal freedom and patriotism, while critics argue that celebrity endorsements invite scrutiny, particularly when they involve controversial political figures.
Mayweather's boxing legacy and troubles outside the ring

Mayweather's sporting achievements remain difficult to dispute. He retired from professional boxing with an undefeated 50-0 record, having beaten a long list of prominent opponents during a career that included championship victories across multiple weight divisions.
His defensive technique, timing and ability to control fights made him one of the defining boxers of his generation.
He has remained involved in boxing since his professional retirement in 2017, particularly through exhibition events. Yet his plans for further appearances have encountered complications in 2026.
An exhibition against Greek kickboxing star Mike Zambidis , scheduled for June in Athens, was called off amid a legal dispute involving CSI Sports Events.
The company alleged that Mayweather's agreements to fight Mike Tyson and Manny Pacquiao created contractual restrictions on competing in other events first.
Those claims were part of a legal dispute, rather than a finding that Mayweather had committed wrongdoing. The proposed Pacquiao rematch was also pushed into uncertainty.

Mayweather has also faced scrutiny over financial matters. In April 2026, The Ring reported that the IRS had notified him of its intention to alert the State Department about a possible passport revocation related to an unresolved tax debt. That development threatened to complicate his international exhibition plans.
Those issues have contributed to the broader attention surrounding Mayweather , although they are separate from his political endorsement.
The fact that he continues to attract headlines across sport, business and politics reflects his unusual position as a globally recognised athlete whose public life extends far beyond the ring.

Ultimately, Mayweather's appearance in Arizona has reopened the debate over how much influence celebrities should wield in political conversations. His supporters are entitled to view his endorsement as a personal expression of patriotism, while critics remain free to challenge his judgment and political choices.
The backlash may continue online, but it does not change the central point: Mayweather has made his support for Trump public, and the reaction shows that his words still command attention.

articles.title: De la Hoya slams Canelo for going ahead with his fight in Saudi Arabia in the middle of a conflict: “They say he's not afraid...”
articles.standfirst: The Golden Boy promoter has urged Turki Alalshikh to reconsider the October 31 event
articles.summary: The Golden Boy promoter has urged Turki Alalshikh to reconsider the October 31 event
articles.body:
Oscar De La Hoya has criticized Canelo Alvarez for remaining committed to his October 31 fight against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, despite growing security concerns linked to regional hostilities.

The former world champion believes the financial interests surrounding the event shouldn’t come before the safety of fighters, staff and spectators.

Speaking on his Clap Back Thursdays segment, De La Hoya directed his frustration at Alvarez, Turki Alalshikh and event organizer SELA.

His comments followed reports of deadly attacks involving Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, prompting questions about whether the city can safely host a major international sporting event.

Alalshikh has maintained that the fight will go ahead as scheduled, claiming Alvarez personally contacted him to confirm his commitment. However, De La Hoya believes the Mexican superstar’s willingness to compete doesn’t address the potential dangers facing everyone else travelling to Saudi Arabia.

“He says Canelo has no fear. Well, Canelo might not have any fear because he’s flying into a private airport,” said De La Hoya.

“But what about everyone else associated with the event? They’re scared sh*tless. How is this event not cancelled? It’s a f**king enormous safety concern.”

De La Hoya questions safety as Riyadh sporting events face disruption

De La Hoya said he wouldn’t travel to a conflict zone under the same circumstances and called on organizers to consider relocating the contest.

He pointed to the postponement of Riyadh’s Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition, which was moved from October to December, as an example of how sporting schedules can change when circumstances warrant reconsideration.

He also accused Alalshikh and SELA of exerting excessive influence over boxing media. Those allegations remain De La Hoya’s claims, and his longstanding disagreements with Alvarez and Saudi boxing officials provide important context for his latest remarks.

Nevertheless, the safety debate goes beyond the headline fighters. Undercard boxers, trainers, cutmen, production crews, journalists and spectators all have different travel arrangements and security needs.

While a superstar might have access to private transport and additional protection, other participants may have fewer options if conditions deteriorate.

Fans could also face significant financial losses if travel plans are disrupted, particularly after paying for flights, accommodation and tickets. These practical concerns add another dimension to De La Hoya’s argument that organizers should carefully assess the risks before proceeding.

Alvarez has been working towards his return following his September 2025 defeat to Terence Crawford and subsequent elbow surgery.

A matchup with Mbilli would offer him an opportunity to re-enter the super middleweight title picture, while Mbilli would receive a major platform against one of boxing’s biggest names.

However, the sporting significance of the contest hasn’t removed the uncertainty surrounding its location. De La Hoya believes organizers should prioritize human safety over the substantial financial interests involved.

As fight night approaches, attention remains focused on whether the event will proceed as planned or whether organisers will reconsider their arrangements.

articles.title: Dubois retains the heavyweight title after a commanding victory over Wardley
articles.standfirst: The boxer defeated his compatriot by technical knockout in the second round
articles.summary: The boxer defeated his compatriot by technical knockout in the second round
articles.body:
The British boxer Daniel Dubois retained his World Boxing Organization heavyweight title after a commanding victory over Fabio Wardley by technical knockout in the second round. This fight, held at London’s O2 Arena, was dubbed by many as the "fight of the year" and ended with a fierce attack from the champion.

In the first round, Dubois needed just 17 seconds to send his compatriot to the canvas with a right hand over the guard. That dominance was also evident in the second round: with 39 seconds left before the end, referee Steve Gray stopped the fight just as Wardley’s trainer, Ben Davison, was throwing in the towel.

Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) thus achieved a devastating victory, with which he wanted to send a clear message to the rest of the fighters in the division. "It was my moment and this is my era," Dubois told the AP news agency. "We just had to go out there and show that we meant business; that was exactly what we did."

'This marks the second defeat in Wardley's professional career (20-2-1, 19 KOs). "It's never pleasant to lose, but it is what it is. That's this sport," Wardley said.'

articles.title: Michael Beasley defeats Delonte West via first round TKO in clash of former NBA veterans
articles.standfirst: The former NBA players met at Adin Ross' Miami event
articles.summary: The former NBA players met at Adin Ross' Miami event
articles.body:
What was billed as an unusual meeting between two former NBA players ended in just 38 seconds on Friday night, leaving Michael Beasley celebrating a victory and Delonte West facing renewed concern over his wellbeing.

The former basketball veterans stepped into the ring at streamer Adin Ross' Brand Risk 16 event in Miami, but their boxing contest barely lasted long enough to develop into a competitive exchange.

Beasley , 37, secured a first-round technical knockout after connecting with a right hand that sent West to the canvas, prompting the referee to intervene when his opponent struggled to recover.

The result immediately generated criticism online, with viewers questioning the decision to stage the fight given West's difficult circumstances since leaving professional basketball.

West approached his boxing debut aggressively, advancing toward Beasley from the opening bell while throwing a series of heavy punches.

However, his attacks frequently left him off balance, allowing the younger former NBA forward to maintain his composure and capitalize on an opening.

Beasley eventually landed a clean right hand that knocked West down, with the referee beginning a count as the 43-year-old attempted to regain his footing.

The official stopped the contest after just 38 seconds, although confusion followed when the ring announcer mistakenly identified West as the winner.

The error was subsequently corrected, confirming Beasley 's victory in a contest that had already attracted considerable attention because of the circumstances surrounding his opponent.

West's boxing debut prompts concern

West spent eight NBA seasons with the Boston Celtics, Cleveland Cavaliers and Dallas Mavericks , establishing himself as a capable guard before his final league appearance in 2012.

Since leaving professional basketball, the former first-round draft pick has faced significant personal challenges, including substance abuse, periods of homelessness and struggles with his mental health.

His difficulties have been widely documented, making his appearance in a celebrity boxing event particularly concerning to some viewers following Friday's rapid stoppage.

West was also arrested in Virginia earlier this year following an alleged robbery involving $23, according to TMZ, before being released on a $1,000 bond.

That incident was unrelated to the boxing match, but his recent circumstances contributed to questions about whether organizers had adequately considered his welfare.

Adin Ross responds to criticism

Ross addressed the backlash during his livestream, defending the decision to include West and emphasizing that the former NBA player had received financial compensation.

"I made sure he got paid well," Ross said, explaining that he wanted to provide West with an opportunity to improve his personal circumstances.

However, the streamer's explanation did little to satisfy critics who questioned whether the financial benefits outweighed the potential risks associated with the contest.

Some viewers characterized the matchup as exploitative, while others raised concerns about the medical clearance required before West was permitted to compete.

Although Beasley emerged victorious, the conversation surrounding the event has focused less on his performance than on the responsibilities involved in organizing celebrity boxing matches.

articles.standfirst: Saúl Álvarez opened up about poverty, financial literacy and managing money. Here’s what he said and how much his fortune is estimated to be worth.
articles.summary: Saúl Álvarez opened up about poverty, financial literacy and managing money. Here’s what he said and how much his fortune is estimated to be worth.
articles.body:
Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez went from selling popsicles on buses in Jalisco as a child to becoming one of Mexico’s highest-paid athletes. His remarkable rise also transformed his relationship with money and business, a subject he discussed in an interview that sparked controversy.

Speaking with Oso Trava on the Cracks Podcast, the boxing champion opened up about poverty, financial literacy and investing. One comment in particular sparked debate: “Money always runs out. I’ve always said poor people will always be poor because they choose to be.” But what exactly did Canelo mean?

CanCanelo Álvarez’s perspective stems from his own experience managing large sums of money. As he explained, suddenly coming into a fortune does not necessarily mean knowing how to manage it or make it last.

According to Canelo, the problem begins when people try to maintain a lifestyle they can no longer afford.

Canelo Álvarez also recalled that he went through periods when he spent a significant portion of his wealth. After accumulating between $5 million and $10 million, he said he made several purchases and bought properties until he was left with around $100,000. Those experiences helped shape his financial philosophy, which focuses on several key principles:

1. Investing in assets rather than relying solely on money in the bank.

2. Generating a steady cash flow.

3. Diversifying through different businesses.

4- Protecting his reputation and the value of his name.

5. Turning to real estate as an initial investment.

His criticism also extended to other boxers who, in his view, spend as if their income will last forever. “Boxing is temporary,” he said, stressing the importance of investing while earnings are high.

How much is Canelo Álvarez worth?

Available estimates put Canelo Álvarez’s net worth at more than $290 million, although that figure is based on estimates and may change as his earnings and investments evolve.

Outside boxing, the Guadalajara native has built businesses in industries including gas stations, beverages, restaurants, automobiles and real estate. His business ventures have become an important part of his overall wealth.

In 2023, Forbes estimated that Canelo earned around $110 million that year, putting him among the world’s highest-paid athletes. Now, Canelo is preparing for his fight against Mbilli.

Canelo Álvarez’s journey shows that boxing earnings can also provide the foundation for other business ventures. And as he continues to combine boxing with investments and entrepreneurship, his business empire could keep growing long after he hangs up his gloves.

articles.title: Who is Christian Mbilli: Age, where he's from, nickname, and everything about Canelo Álvarez's next opponent
articles.standfirst: Mbilli has an important professional boxing career.
articles.summary: Mbilli has an important professional boxing career.
articles.body:
Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez returns to the ring before retiring permanently from professional boxing and ending his career on a high note. His opponent will be Christian Mbilli , a French fighter with Cameroonian roots, who will not make things easy for his Mexican opponent in the upcoming fight.

It is a powerful opponent, who has experience in the ring, so it will not be an easy or routine fight for Canelo Álvarez , who knows he is in the final stretch of his career. This bout has generated a lot of expectations in Mexico and among the elite of international boxing.

That is why below on MARCA MX we will tell you more about Christian Mbilli, such as his nickname, his record, and his fighting style, since this fighter will look to defeat Canelo Álvarez in his return to boxing.

Christian Mbilli is a French boxer born on April 26, 1995, who competes in the super middleweight division and has significant achievements in his career, although his name has gained prominence since he agreed to be Canelo Álvarez's next opponent.

Nicknamed The Panther or The Killer Panther , Mbilli will look to hand the Mexican another defeat in his career, which would tarnish Canelo Álvarez's retirement and put to rest the rumors that the Mexican would choose favorable opponents for the final stage of his career as a professional boxer.

This French fighter comes into his fight against Canelo Álvarez undefeated, with a record of 29 wins, 0 losses, and 1 draw, along with a high knockout rate of around 80%, so on paper, he could be the favorite in this fight.

Before turning professional, he represented France at the Rio 2016 Olympic Games in the middleweight division, reaching the quarterfinals. He later began his career with fights in Canada.

In fact, in January of this year he was named World Boxing Council (WBC) super middleweight world champion.

His fighting style can be defined as that of a boxer who likes to pressure his opponent and an aggressive slugger. His strategy in the ring does not focus on tactical subtlety or footwork, but rather on physically and mentally overwhelming his rivals through sheer endurance and a high volume of punches.

When is the Canelo Álvarez vs Christian Mbilli fight?

The Canelo Álvarez vs Christian Mbilli fight is scheduled for next Saturday, October 31, right on Halloween night.

This fight will take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia and there is great anticipation to see Canelo Álvarez's return.

articles.title: Social media bombshell: Ryan Garcia claims Floyd Mayweather will come out of retirement for a real fight at 147 pounds
articles.standfirst: The reigning WBC welterweight champion says he and the undefeated boxing legend have agreed to a professional showdown, but Mayweather has yet to publicly confirm the deal
articles.summary: The reigning WBC welterweight champion says he and the undefeated boxing legend have agreed to a professional showdown, but Mayweather has yet to publicly confirm the deal
articles.body:
R yan Garcia has sent the boxing world into a frenzy after claiming that Floyd Mayweather has agreed to return to professional competition for a fight at 147 pounds, with the WBC welterweight championship potentially on the line.

The 28-year-old American revealed the news through social media, insisting that the proposed matchup would be a genuine professional contest rather than another exhibition.

Garcia also shared a screenshot of a FaceTime conversation with Mayweather, offering what he presented as evidence that discussions had taken place.

"Trust me at first I thought this was bull***," Garcia announced on social media. "But it’s real Floyd and I agree to a fight."

"147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world," the 28-year-old boxing superstar added, saying, "50-0 vs The current champ."

The announcement immediately raised the possibility of one of boxing's most intriguing generational matchups. Garcia is an active champion entering his prime, while Mayweather has not competed in a sanctioned professional bout since defeating Conor McGregor in 2017.

However, there is an important distinction between Garcia's announcement and a formally confirmed fight. Mayweather has not publicly verified the agreement, and no official date, venue or broadcast arrangements have been announced.

Reports published after Garcia's posts also indicated that the status of negotiations remained uncertain.

Garcia wants Mayweather's unbeaten record on the line

The biggest selling point of the proposed matchup is the possibility that Mayweather's famous 50-0 professional record could finally be put at risk.

Throughout his career, Mayweather built his reputation on defensive brilliance, ring intelligence and an ability to neutralize opponents with different fighting styles.

He won world titles across five weight divisions before stepping away from professional boxing following his victory over McGregor , the former UFC champion, in August 2017.

That contest generated enormous commercial interest, with Mayweather stopping McGregor in the 10th round to secure his 50th professional win. Since then, the American has participated in exhibition bouts, but those appearances have not affected his official record.

Garcia , meanwhile, has made it clear that an exhibition would not satisfy his ambitions. He wants the contest recognized as a professional fight, with the potential consequences that come with a sanctioned championship bout.

The Californian claimed the WBC welterweight title by defeating Mario Barrios in February 2026. He subsequently defended the belt against Conor Benn in September, strengthening his position in the division ahead of a possible blockbuster encounter.

A fight at 147 pounds would place Garcia's championship at the center of the discussion. Nevertheless, the WBC would still need to address the relevant sanctioning requirements before the matchup could be treated as an officially approved world-title contest.

Mayweather's age and lengthy absence raise questions

While Garcia is an active fighter, Mayweather is approaching a significant milestone. The former five-division world champion turns 50 in February 2027, meaning the age difference between the pair would be considerable if they eventually meet.

Mayweather's experience and defensive skills would make him a major attraction regardless of the circumstances. Yet returning to a professional ring against a much younger champion would represent a very different challenge from participating in an exhibition.

The former champion has previously expressed interest in returning to professional boxing, and a comeback has been discussed in connection with other high-profile matchups.

A proposed rematch with Manny Pacquiao has also been part of the wider conversation surrounding his future, although that contest has faced complications.

There are also practical questions to resolve. A verbal agreement, even if both fighters have genuinely expressed interest, does not establish that contracts have been signed or that regulators have approved the contest.

The absence of confirmation from Mayweather is particularly significant. Until he addresses Garcia's announcement and the necessary arrangements become public, fans have reason to approach the claims cautiously.

Could this become boxing's biggest fight of the year?

The commercial appeal is easy to understand. Garcia brings youth, speed, punching power and a substantial social media following, while Mayweather remains one of the sport's most recognizable names.

Their contrasting careers would make the buildup almost as compelling as the contest itself.

For Garcia , defeating Mayweather would be a career-defining achievement, even if critics inevitably debated the significance of beating a fighter returning at nearly 50 years old.

For Mayweather , the stakes would be different: losing a sanctioned professional bout would bring his unblemished record to an end.

That possibility is precisely what separates Garcia's proposed fight from the exhibitions that have defined much of Mayweather's post-retirement activity.

For now, the boxing community must wait for more concrete information. Garcia has made his position clear and has publicly claimed that both men have agreed to fight, but a confirmed event still requires further details and official approval.

If the announcement develops into a signed, sanctioned contest at 147 pounds, the matchup could become one of boxing's most talked-about events.

Until then, the prospect of Mayweather risking his perfect record against the current WBC champion remains an intriguing possibility rather than a finalized fight.

articles.title: Terence Crawford backs a clear winner in the Canelo Álvarez vs Christian Mbilli fight
articles.standfirst: He believes Mbilli’s style is tailor-made for the Mexican to secure a convincing victory
articles.summary: He believes Mbilli’s style is tailor-made for the Mexican to secure a convincing victory
articles.body:
S aúl Canelo Álvarez is preparing to return to the ring on October 31 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The Mexican will face French-Cameroonian Christian Mbilli in a super middleweight bout that will mark his 69th professional appearance .

The fight comes more than a year after his last appearance, the one in which he lost the division titles to Terence Crawford by unanimous decision in September 2025 .

Crawford sees it as a favorable fight for Canelo to prevail

Crawford, the man who took the belts from Canelo, knows the tapatío's style, strengths, and also weaknesses firsthand. The American, considered one of the best boxers of his generation and a champion in multiple divisions, has closely followed Álvarez's return and did not hesitate to offer a detailed analysis of what he expects to see in Saudi Arabia.

For “Bud,” Mbilli’s style is ideal for Canelo to win clearly . “Mbilli’s style is perfect and he won’t be able to do anything when Canelo applies pressure; I don’t see any chance for him to win,” Crawford said.

In his view, the Mexican’s constant pressure, his body work, and his experience in high-level fights will end up nullifying the undefeated Frenchman’s options and will leave an unquestionable result in Riyadh.

The context of the Canelo-Crawford rivalry

Canelo's defeat to Crawford remains his most recent official memory in the ring. That night in Las Vegas, the Nebraskan dominated the scorecards and took all the 168-pound titles .

Canelo has not made excuses about the result, although he has acknowledged on more than one occasion that he did not arrive in his best physical or mental condition . His trainer, Eddy Reynoso, was even more direct when asked about a possible rematch: “It would be against Terence Crawford, definitely”.

Since then, Canelo underwent elbow surgery, completed a long rehabilitation process, and set up a demanding training camp in Valencia , Spain, away from the usual bustle. The objective is clear: to show that he still has the level to compete among the elite of the super middleweight division and recover the ground he has lost.

Mbilli, the undefeated challenger

Christian Mbilli comes in with a solid record and the reputation of being an aggressive, pressure fighter with good knockout power. However, Crawford believes that precisely this style of constant forward pressure is what suits Canelo best , a boxer who has historically punished those who come at him and who knows how to manage distance and timing like few others .

The fight will take place under the promotion of Turki Alalshikh and will be part of a stacked card. On the same event, Jaime Munguía will fight defending his super middleweight crown, Rafael “Divino” Espinoza and Alan David “Rey” Picasso .

"Crawford, from a distance and with the authority of someone who has already defeated Canelo, painted a forceful scenario : the Mexican applying pressure, Mbilli with no clear answers, and a result that, according to his analysis, leaves no room for doubt. There is little time left for the Riyadh ring to confirm or disprove the current champion’s prediction.

Key facts about the Canelo - Mbilli fight

Fight: Canelo Álvarez vs Christian Mbilli (super middleweight).

Date and venue: October 31, 2026 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Canelo's last fight: Loss by unanimous decision to Terence Crawford (September 2025).

Crawford's prediction: Canelo wins; he doesn't see Mbilli as having a chance.

articles.summary: A viral moment brought unexpected attention
articles.body:
L ucero “La Loba” Acosta’s Professional Fighters League debut ended with a third-round loss to Shannon Clark. But after a wardrobe mishap during the televised fight went viral, Lucero turned the attention toward her OnlyFans account and shared a figure that left fans wondering how much the moment was worth.

The bout took place at PFL Chicago on Oct. 16. Clark won by TKO at 1:59 of the third round, handing Acosta her first loss since 2022 and moving her professional record to 6-3.

The $500,000 figure remains unverified

"La Loba" had promising moments early, but Clark’s pressure shifted the fight in her favor. In the third round, Shannon took the Mexican fighter to the canvas and landed a series of strikes. Acosta’s top shifted during the exchange, briefly exposing her, and referee Kevin MacDonald stopped the bout shortly afterward.

The incident quickly drew attention online. Lucero responded on Instagram by connecting the viral moment to a rise in activity on her OnlyFans account. “Extra payment on @onlyfans because we showed our nipples during the @pflmma live,” she wrote, jokingly calling the platform an “official sponsor.”

After the fight , Acosta shared a figure of $500,000 on her Instagram Story, but didn’t explain what it meant. Was it from new OnlyFans subscribers, her total earnings or something else?

It was a tough night in the cage, but the viral moment gave " la Loba" a chance to promote her OnlyFans to a wider audience.

Lucero Acosta joined the PFL after competing for Combate Global and riding a four-fight winning streak. Her last win before the Chicago bout came against Abril Anguiano in April 2025.

After the fight , Acosta shared a figure of $500,000 on her Instagram Story, but didn’t explain what it meant. Was it from new OnlyFans subscribers, her total earnings or something else?
It was a tough night in the cage, but the viral moment gave " la Loba" a chance to promote her OnlyFans to a wider audience.
